svg.title: What USPS pages say about Priority Mail and USPS Ground Advantage: delivery time, size and weight, included insurance and tracking, pickup, hazardous materials, and what the pages do not say.
svg.text: Two USPS services compared
What USPS's pages say, without prices
Delivery time
Priority Mail: expected 2-3 days; the date is on
the receipt or at checkout, with no money-back
guarantee. Ground Advantage: expected 2-5 days;
slower to Alaska, Hawaii, offshore places or
with hazardous materials. Both are expected times.
Size and weight
Both pages: up to 70 lbs. Largest combined
length and girth: 108 inches for Priority
Mail, 130 inches for Ground Advantage.
Priority Mail also has Flat Rate packaging.
Included insurance, with conditions
Priority Mail page: up to $100 with 'most
shipments'. Ground Advantage page: $100 is
included. Insurance page: both need a USPS
Tracking barcode to qualify. More coverage
can be bought, up to $5,000.
Both pages
Free Package Pickup. Tracking is included;
the Priority Mail page excludes Prepaid
Forever Priority Mail Flat Rate.
Hazardous materials
Ground Advantage: primary option for hazmat
that is mailable only on the ground. The
Priority Mail page lists a hazmat handling fee.
Not stated
The Ground Advantage page does not say if its
date has a guarantee or how much slower
service can be. No page shows an update date.
Sources: three USPS.com pages; read Nov. 17, 2026
Prices are not shown.
